items.title: run-generator-gate.ps1 fails its deterministic-generation check, and the differing file is now NAMED for the first time: App\src\main\resources\npdev\support\schema-realization.manifest.json. Two full generations of simple-contact-intake from identical inputs produce byte-different copies of that one file; all other 642 compared files are identical. Diagnosed 2026-07-21 (T7.1) by replicating check-deterministic-generation.ps1's exact scope (ArtifactNP + App, excluding \build\ and npdev-build-info.properties) while retaining per-file hashes — the check itself records only overallStatus plus two file counts, which is why four rounds could carry this without anyone knowing what differed. INTERMITTENT: a first probe over the whole Output tree found this file identical across two runs (its only diff there was Reports\generation-run.json, a pure wall-clock/runId provenance report of the same class as the already-excluded npdev-build-info.properties); a second, correctly-scoped probe reproduced the manifest difference. So it is not deterministic-per-run. NOT attributable to LNCH-1 T2: the failure mode is non-determinism between two runs of the same build, and T2 was a deterministic content change (a literal appended to a List, a fixed string appended to a StringBuilder) introducing no map/set iteration, no filesystem ordering and no clock; a deterministic change cannot make two runs differ from each other. The file's content is entirely static metadata with no timestamp field, so the mechanism is likely an ordering- or environment-sensitive input to whichever emitter writes the npdev/support surface manifest. Next step (do this first, it is cheap): capture BOTH generated copies and diff them — the probe at scratchpad\determinism-probe.ps1 needs only to save file contents, not just hashes. Do not re-derive the attribution from scratch. ROOT CAUSE + FIX 2026-07-21 (T10): captured both copies (D:\WorkSpace\NPDev\Build\lnch1-T10\prefix-run.json) and byte-diffed them — the only difference was the iteration order of the two keys inside the manifest's storageBoundary object (runtimeTables / businessTables). FinalAppAssembler.writeSchemaRealizationManifest built that nested object with java.util.Map.of(...), whose ImmutableCollections.MapN iteration order is randomized per-JVM by ImmutableCollections.SALT; Jackson serializes maps in iteration order, so each fresh-JVM generation emitted the two keys in a run-to-run-varying order (6 pre-fix runs → 2 distinct hashes, 4×orderA / 2×orderB). Fixed by building storageBoundary as an insertion-ordered LinkedHashMap. Proven: 6 post-fix generations all byte-identical (sha256 6415…b0a9), and run-generator-gate.ps1 determinism check now passed (643/643 files, differingFileCount 0). FOLLOW-UP 2026-07-21 (T10 follow-up) — this was a bug CLASS, not one site. The owner flagged that only 1 of 6 multi-entry Map.of(...) sites had been fixed. The other 5 (all in the same two emitter packages): SchemaRealizationEmitter schemaLifecycle / sourceOfTruth / databaseIdentity.dbeaver, and OperationalRunbookEmitter dbeaver / smoke. All 5 converted to insertion-ordered LinkedHashMap (the empty zero-arg Map.of() pair at SchemaRealizationEmitter:1124-1125 left untouched — nothing to iterate). Honest scope correction: unlike the original FinalAppAssembler site (plain new ObjectMapper(), which genuinely flipped run-to-run), both of these emitters' OBJECT_MAPPERs enable ORDER_MAP_ENTRIES_BY_KEYS, which re-sorts every map — nested included — by key at write time, so schema-realization-manifest.json and _ops/resolved-db-plan.json were already byte-deterministic (verified: their output keys are alphabetical at every level). These 5 fixes are therefore latent-hazard removal — they stop the determinism guarantee from silently depending on a global mapper flag (drop the flag and non-determinism returns) — not correction of an active flip. A source-scanning conformance test NoMultiEntryMapOfInGeneratedManifestEmittersTest now scans the assembly/ + dbconfig/ packages (which include FinalAppAssembler, the flag-less emitter that IS actively vulnerable) and fails loudly, naming file+line, if a 7th multi-entry Map.of appears; proven to fail (planted probe → red) and pass (clean → green). Re-proof: 6 separate-process generations (pwsh × 6, each a fresh :generator:run JavaExec JVM) of simple-contact-intake — manifest all 6 sha256 299ea41a…, plan all 6 sha256 9e3a2624…, 1 distinct hash each. Evidence: NPDev_General__OutsideRepo\lnch1-evidence\platcol-T10-followup.md, copies at D:\WorkSpace\NPDev\Build\lnch1-T10-followup\
items.status: **CLOSED (fixed 2026-07-21, T10 + T10 follow-up)** — bug CLASS: 6 multi-entry `Map.of` sites total across `assembly/`+`dbconfig/` emitters; 1 (the active `FinalAppAssembler` flip) fixed in T10, the other 5 (latent, masked today by `ORDER_MAP_ENTRIES_BY_KEYS`) fixed in the follow-up; all now insertion-ordered `LinkedHashMap`; a source-scan conformance test prevents a 7th; re-proven with a 6-run separate-process byte-identical repeat-generation of both affected files

items.title: The determinism check reports only overallStatus + firstFileCount/secondFileCount, never WHICH files differ, so a failure carries no actionable information — that alone is why GATE-DET-1 went four rounds unidentified. It also excludes npdev-build-info.properties by name but not Reports\generation-run.json, which carries the same non-reproducible provenance (generatedAt, timestamp-derived runId); that file is outside the compared roots today, so it is latent rather than active. Make the check name the differing paths in its report. items.title: The governance realignment itself. The 6 sub-checks above encode the pre-d0bf41b "package == support bucket" convention that the beta-0 manifest refactor replaced with exact lists, so they measure a convention the codebase no longer follows. Either realign the checks to the exact-list model or retire them. Diagnosis (T5, 2026-07-21): governance/evidence drift, NOT a code defect — run-runtimehost-gate.ps1 already invoked run-runtime-surface-evidence.ps1 with -PendingOk for exactly these checks, calling them advisory, while the observability step re-read the same report files and treated them as blocking; the gate contradicted itself. runtime-surface-allowlist-report.json — the report backing real build-time allowlist enforcement — is passed, so nothing is actually unguarded. run-observability-hardening.ps1 now accepts these 6 named checks as advisory via -SurfaceConvergencePendingOk, and only when they are the sole failures: any other failing sub-check in any of the three surface reports still fails the gate loudly. DECISION (REG-5, 2026-07-21): option (b) FORMAL RETIREMENT. Concrete finding that settles the owner question the plan flagged: runtime-surface-allowlist-report.json (backed by RuntimeControllerAllowlistConfig reading npdev/runtime-supported-controllers.json) IS the exact-list-model enforcement the beta-0 refactor introduced, it is BLOCKING, and it passes. The 6 package-convention convergence/exclusivity checks are a redundant proxy for the superseded 'package == support bucket' rule -- a rewrite 'against the exact-list model' (the plan's default option a) would only duplicate the allowlist. They are retired to informational-only (never a gate blocker), reversible if the governance model changes. Implemented in run-observability-hardening.ps1 (header + message reworded from 'advisory pending owner' to 'retired/superseded') and run-runtimehost-gate.ps1. 'Advisory, unowned' is no longer the state.

CORRECTED 2026-07-21 (REG-3) — the original "policy conflict" framing on this row was wrong, and is preserved here only so the misdiagnosis is not re-derived a third time. It claimed the workspace-slimness policy and run-beta-release-gate.ps1 were in structural tension because the json-schema-validator-tests report needs node_modules present while the slimness hook refuses a commit while it exists. That tension has not existed since commit 437d19b ("Keep schema validator dependencies outside workspace", 2026-05-14) — two months before this row was written. The validator's node_modules now lives OUTSIDE the repo at ..\NPDev_General__OutsideRepo\node-tools\json-schema-validator, provisioned on demand by scripts/quality/Invoke-JsonSchemaValidation.ps1 when missing or when the lockfile fingerprint changes; scripts/hygiene/Test-WorkspaceSlimness.ps1 only scans the in-repo workspace root and cannot see it. docs/WORKSPACE_CLEANUP_POLICY.md documents this as the required pattern. There is no decision for an owner to make and nothing to exempt. The real defect, now fixed: the gate is an evidence aggregator over 36 requiredReports produced by ~18 separate scripts, and nothing ever ran those producers as a set — so a clean-tree run exited 1 with 35 of 36 reports simply absent and zero reports actually failing, which the gate reported identically to a real release failure. That ambiguity is what let the wrong diagnosis stand. Fixed 2026-07-21: (1) new scripts/quality/run-beta-release-evidence-orchestration.ps1 runs every producer in dependency-ordered stages sharing one -RunId (the gate's single-runId rule is otherwise unsatisfiable by hand); (2) run-beta-release-gate.ps1 gained an opt-in -GenerateReports switch that invokes it, kept opt-in because producing the full set builds and boots applications; (3) the gate now distinguishes precondition-unmet from check-failed — exit 2 + a leading PRECONDITION-UNMET: line when required evidence was never generated (explicitly not a release failure), exit 1 + CHECK-FAILED: when evidence exists and something it asserts is broken, exit 0 on pass; a new evidencePreconditions block in the report splits the blocker list into the two classes. A found-on-the-way producer defect was fixed in its own commit (deccf87): run-json-schema-validator-tests.ps1 threw on first failure with a hardcoded overallStatus="passed", so it could only ever emit passing evidence or none — the producer-level form of the same conflation — and its official-model-extra-property-invalid fixture had gone stale (every property it relied on had since been legitimately added to model.schema.json's 26 root properties), silently disabling the model-root additionalProperties:false guard

items.title: CLOSED (2026-07-21, REG-2/P2 + REG-9/P3). Root cause was neither prior theory NOR the plans Hikari candidate. Reproduced RED first (Docker up, Testcontainers Postgres 15) against the assembled simple-user-registry app and captured the exact chain: Caused by: java.lang.IllegalStateException: Configured database is npdev_sample_postgres, but connected database is test at DatabaseIdentityStartupValidator.mismatch(:81). The DataSource IS created (theory 2 wrong); the validator obtains it, runs select current_database(), and the Testcontainers jdbc:tc:postgresql URL always reports the container default name test, which never equals the apps resolved identity - so context load aborts, presenting from outside as an opaque ApplicationContext failure (mis-attributed twice). Fix (profile/config level, not per-IT DataSource): application-postgres.yml now sets npdev.trial.database-override: true, the validators existing purpose-built bypass whose own doc comment describes exactly this "a profile intentionally substituted a fixed database" case. Findings surfaced once the tests ran (plan Sec 7.3 step 5): (a) PublicationRollbackE2EIT queried WHERE publication_execution_id = CAST(? AS uuid) but that platform-owned column is TEXT (every npdev_ id column is) - Postgres rejects text = uuid, H2 silently coerced it; fixed the cast. (b) JwtAuthExternalBetaIT x8 crashed at context load because LoginController hard-required a JWT signing key in a verify-only profile - fixed under REG-9/P3 (LoginController tolerates a blank private-key-path). Run recipe (from the assembled app root, Docker running): ./gradlew.bat integrationTest --tests com.finalexec.TenantIsolationE2EIT --tests com.finalexec.PublicationRollbackE2EIT --tests com.finalexec.JwtAuthExternalBetaIT -PnpdevRuntimeHostLibsDir=D:\WorkSpace\NPDev\Build\runtimehost-libs --no-daemon. On Windows the build auto-sets DOCKER_HOST to the Docker Desktop npipe. Result: 10 tests, 0 failures. Evidence: NPDev_General__OutsideRepo\reg2-evidence\ (red-tenantisolation, green-all-ten-final)

items.title: Flows had branch/if but no iteration (Procedures already looped via forEach/loop → FOR_EACH). Now: a forEach flow step (collection/itemKey/nested steps/maxLoopIterations) compiles, validates (itemKey
items.notes: Flows had branch/if but no iteration (Procedures already looped via forEach/loop → FOR_EACH). Now: a forEach flow step (collection/itemKey/nested steps/maxLoopIterations) compiles, validates (itemKey can't shadow reserved flow state or its own collection root or an enclosing loop's itemKey; nested await rejected — durable resume of an in-flight await inside an iteration is deferred), and executes durably: KernelRunner.executeForEachStep treats the whole loop as one atomic top-level step position, checkpointing iteration progress into state via the existing StepProgressRecorder without advancing the outer step index, so a crash mid-loop resumes at the right iteration with no duplicated side effects — proven by a genuine crash simulation (freezing the executing thread forever right after a durable checkpoint write, then resuming on a brand-new KernelRunner sharing only the store). CompiledModelFlowDefinitionProvider projects it for generated apps (confirmed live: a forEach flow boots inside a real packaged FinalApp); the flow builder gained the first nested step-list editor in ui-react (branch's then had never been rendered either) for authoring the loop body inline.
